approach: Convert all I/O-bound steps to async using AsyncOpenAI, httpx.AsyncClient, asyncio.to_thread for ChromaDB
rationale: Pipeline was ~57 min worst case due to sequential HTTP calls. Async with semaphore-based concurrency provides ~5x speedup with minimal architecture changes.
alternatives_rejected: aiohttp + aiolimiter (adds inconsistent second HTTP client)
anyio wrapping for ChromaDB (over-engineering, asyncio.to_thread works fine)
outcome: All 7 tasks complete. 58 tests passing. Expected ~57min → ~11min pipeline time.

task: Cloudflare bypass strategy for s1 crawler
approach: 3-tier fallback chain in _crawl_one: httpx (fast) → Playwright headless Chromium (CF bypass) → Wayback Machine (last resort). Site-level flag skips httpx after first CF detection.
rationale: Cloudflare-protected sites (carta.com) return 403 to all httpx requests. Playwright is already in requirements.txt. Wayback Machine provides historical content as last resort.
alternatives_rejected: cloudscraper library (fragile, constantly breaks as CF updates)
Proxy rotation (cost, complexity, still blocked by JS challenge)
Skip CF-protected sites (unacceptable — Carta is a client)
outcome: Implementation complete. Awaiting live test on carta.com.

approach: 4-stage async pipeline: Strategic Planner (Sonnet) → Orchestrator-Workers (Sonnet/Haiku/Perplexity) → Evaluator-Optimizer (4 dimensions, 2 revision cycles) → LangGraph HITL. Raw AsyncAnthropic SDK, semaphore concurrency, Langfuse tracing.
rationale: Follows two proven Anthropic patterns: Orchestrator-Workers for parallel content production, Evaluator-Optimizer for automated QA. Reuses existing async/semaphore patterns from gap analysis. LangGraph HITL matches research pipeline pattern.
alternatives_rejected: LangChain wrappers (inconsistent with gap analysis, hides control)
Single monolithic LLM call (no quality control, no parallelism)
outcome: Full implementation complete. 57/57 tests passing. 30+ files created across core/content_engine/, tests/content_engine/, scripts/.

task: Codex review findings incorporated into content engine plan
approach: Incorporated 8 critical findings from Codex o3 review: return_exceptions=True in gather, safe_parse() for LLM JSON, retry for Anthropic errors, context window guard, directory creation, early exit for max_revision_cycles=0, StructuralTargets model, word_count_range tuple.
rationale: Codex identified real edge cases and alignment issues with the architecture doc that would have caused bugs in production.
outcome: All 8 findings implemented in the codebase.

task: FastAPI integration architecture — asyncio.create_task, JSON TaskStore, SSE events, MemorySaver HITL
approach: Same-repo api/ package. asyncio.create_task (not Celery), JSON-file-backed TaskStore, SSE for progress, MemorySaver checkpointer for HITL interrupt/resume. pydantic_settings.BaseSettings for env-var config.
rationale: Lightweight, no infra deps. JSON files are simple and debuggable. asyncio.create_task matches existing async-first patterns. MemorySaver enables LangGraph checkpoint/resume for HITL approvals.
alternatives_rejected: WebSocket for progress (SSE is simpler, auto-reconnect via Last-Event-ID)
SQLite TaskStore (unnecessary complexity, JSON files are sufficient)
outcome: 6 phases complete. 126 tests passing. All 3 pipelines wrapped with REST endpoints, SSE events, and HITL approval flow.
